initial.text: Retry only retryable failures, within a fixed budget
Cedar Relay
Permanent failures stop immediately; retryable failures use increasing requested delays without a delivery deduplication guarantee.
Fictional source change and deterministic modeled examples
A rejected acknowledgment can still follow a committed remote effect.
The setting
The old loop retried every rejection
The old loop retried rejected sends until the retry budget ran out. It requested a ten-millisecond delay between attempts.
The change
Classify failures before waiting

The changed loop stops on a non-retryable error. Otherwise it requests delays of 10, 20, then 40 milliseconds as the attempt index increases. A budget of two retries permits up to three sends. A rejected sleep prevents the next send.
The boundary
A retry can duplicate a remote effect

The author describes exactly-once delivery, but the supplied contract permits a send to reject after its effect commits. The modeled lost-acknowledgment example records two effects. Separate invocations share no retry budget or exclusion mechanism.
The short version
Fewer retries for permanent failures
The change filters failures and increases requested delays. It bounds send attempts per invocation, not successful delivery or duplicate effects.

initial.text: Publish only after the payment transaction commits
Lantern Ledger
A failed commit now prevents publication, while publication failure leaves a committed payment intact.
Fictional source change and deterministic modeled examples
The supplied code has no durable outbox or delivery deduplication.
The setting
Publication used to precede commit
The old callback marked the payment and published before the transaction committed. In the modeled commit failure, a notification escaped while the database write rolled back.
The change
Wait for the transaction to fulfill
The changed function awaits the transaction before invoking publish. A write or commit rejection therefore prevents publication in that invocation.
The boundary
The database cannot roll back publication failures

The author calls payment and notification atomic, but publish remains an external operation. Its rejection after commit leaves the payment recorded. It may also have delivered a notification before rejecting. The contract allows a process to stop between operations and supplies no durable retry. Concurrent invocations can each publish despite idempotent payment writes.
The short version
Commit first, with a remaining delivery gap
The change prevents publication before a failed commit. It does not make the committed payment and the external notification atomic.

initial.text: Invalidate after a successful write, with a remaining reader race
Moss Catalog
Post-write deletion removes cache fills that finish during the write, but an older in-flight snapshot can refill the cache afterward.
Fictional source change and deterministic modeled examples
The model uses one shared Map, without a generation check for readers.
The setting
Early deletion left a window for stale fills
The old update deleted the cached entry before awaiting the database write. A cache miss could read and cache the old stored value during that wait.
The change
Delete only after the write fulfills

The changed update deletes after the write succeeds. It removes an old cache fill that completed during the write. A failed write leaves an existing cached entry in place. In the sequential example, the next read sees the new stored value.
The boundary
An older snapshot can arrive after deletion

The author says concurrent stale reads are removed, but read is unchanged. The modeled reader captures the old database value, waits through the update and deletion, then caches that old value. A subsequent read returns the stale entry. The change supplies no generation check or in-flight reader synchronization.
The short version
Close one cache-fill window
Moving deletion after a successful write closes the window for fills that finish during that write. It does not prevent stale results from overlapping readers or late cache fills.
